learning: If max_error falls below 0.06 m on s-bend and slalom while steering_oscillation stays near 0.3, the inertia limit was real. If oscillation rises while max_error does not move, the bottleneck is controller gain (kd and kp) for this lighter robot, and I should retune the controller rather than change the geometry.
notes: Complete robot for the Builder's iteration 5 geometry: the iteration 4 design with mass reduced from 0.6 to 0.5 kg. The controller is identical to iteration 4 so the mass change is the only variable. Nothing about this robot's performance has been measured yet.
rationale: Iteration 4 is the best design so far (score 372.6): 5 sensors at y=0.07 m, 16 mm footprint, track 0.10 m, wheel radius 0.040 m, mass 0.6 kg. Its oval finish rate was 80% at 1.875 s mean time, but s-bend and slalom still reached the 0.06 m off-track limit (max_error 0.063 and 0.066). Iteration 3 showed that adding sensors and moving them to y=0.08 m raised oscillation and lowered the oval finish rate, so I keep the iteration 4 sensor layout. The Builder's single-variable test is mass 0.6 to 0.5 kg. Yaw inertia falls by about 17%, so the bends should be tracked with less lag. Lower inertia also makes the same gains respond faster, which may add oscillation. I therefore keep the iteration 4 controller unchanged (kp 3.5, ki 0.05, kd 0.5, base_speed 1.6, weights [-2,-1,0,1,2], last_direction). That isolates the mass change, so any shift in results can be attributed to it. Expected result: s-bend and slalom max_error below the 0.06 m limit with fewer slalom line losses, and an oval finish rate of at least 80%. I have not measured this and do not state an outcome.
